title: Investigation into the protective effects of apple juice on the intestinal barrier in athletes
summary:
In this research project, the influence of acute supplementation of a polyphenol-containing fruit juice drink (naturally cloudy apple juice) and acute physical exertion on the permeability of the intestinal barrier will be investigated. 
The topic of altered gut permeability in the context of exercise is currently a hot topic of research. The effect of physical activity on the permeability of the intestinal barrier has already been investigated in this context. 
However, possible positive effects of a polyphenol-containing fruit juice drink (naturally cloudy apple juice), which also has a positive influence on training responsiveness and regeneration after sport, have not yet been explicitly investigated in combination with acute stress. Polyphenols, which occur as secondary ingredients in fruit juices, are said to have antioxidant, chemopreventive, antibacterial, antiviral, anti-inflammatory and antidiabetic effects. Therefore, in an experimental intervention study, various metabolites in the blood are to be determined and analysed at certain times of the day.

interventions.name: Control group - after endurance exercise they receive 500ml of water
Control group 2: receive 500ml soft drink after endurance exercise
Intervention group: receive 500ml of apple juice spritzer after endurance exercise.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
healthy endurance athletes with an age of 18-60 years
Exclusion criteria:
Hormone substitution; incl. thyroid Hormone therapy
Smokers
One-sided diet (e.g. vegan) 
People in need of treatment 
Cardiac arrhythmia Heart failure (EF<55)
Performance-limiting pAVK  (Fontaine stage ≥ II)
Performance- or training-limiting degenerative joint diseases or muscular diseases
Performance-limiting kidney disease
Performance-limiting neurological disease
oncological diseases in the history (< 5 years)
Psychiatric and/or addictive disorders
